subject: lion
pitch: A proud old lion resting with his head held high. A huge shaggy mane fading from golden blond at the face to dark chocolate at the edges, a tawny body with a pale cream belly and muzzle, amber eyes, a broad black nose, a scar across one eyebrow, big padded paws and a long tail ending in a dark tuft.
reasoning:
I'm designing a resting lion in a sphinx pose, planning realistic proportions and a skeleton hierarchy starting from the pelvis joint through a spine chain.

Then I continue mapping out the neck-to-head connection, jaw, tail chain, and leg placement for front legs extended and hind legs folded, while planning to build the mane from tufted geometry pieces colored with a continuous gradient paint based on distance from the face center. I'm pinning down exact coordinates for the torso, neck, head, and muzzle to keep proportions anatomically plausible.

Mapping spine, neck, and head joint chain...

I'll separate the neck chain into two joints, add a head joint angled slightly up and forward, and a jaw joint positioned near the back of the jaw for hinge rotation. Then I'll set up helper functions for placing box geometries attached to bones with position, color, and rotation parameters.

Now I'm shaping the body using layered ellipsoids: a rear torso near the pelvis bone, a larger chest ellipsoid up front, and a cream-colored belly ellipsoid tucked slightly below and protruding for a lying-down pose.

For the legs, I'm placing the front limbs extended forward with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints positioned so the paws rest flat on the ground, building each as a chain with named points per side.

Writing sweep radii...

I'm adding toe details to the paw with small cream spheres, then setting up a mirror loop for left/right sides, and defining the hind leg chain with hip, knee, hock, and paw joints for the haunch structure.

For the hind foot I need it folded forward alongside the body like a lying lion, so I'm working out the joint positions: thigh angling down to the knee, shin going back to the hock, then the foot sweeping forward to the paw tip, keeping the polyline segments smooth where they skin together.

I'm sizing the hind leg sweep radii and shaping the hind paw as a forward-elongated ellipsoid, plus covering the hip with a haunch ellipsoid. Then I'm plotting the tail chain curving from the pelvis out to the side along the ground, naming the joints tail1 through tail5 and tapering the sweep radius toward the tip.

Adding tail tuft geometry...

Now thinking about the mane: I'll build it as a ring of tufts radiating around the head center and cascading down onto the chest and shoulders.

Still shaping mane tufts...

I'll also add small dark brown fringe tufts under the chest, and set up a paint function that blends gold near the face through rust to dark brown based on distance from the mane center, making sure to pull in the right mix and smoothstep helpers from the SDK without export conflicts.

For the tuft and triangle budget, I'm checking that around 150 tufts at roughly 15 triangles each stays well under part and poly limits. I'm also deciding to paint the body with a countershade function, nesting a mottle pattern for tawny-to-cream variation between the back and belly tones.

Now I'm placing the limb color as a tawny-only mottle, and sketching out the head geometry—skull and muzzle ellipsoids in tawny and cream, cream lip pads as small spheres, and a black wedge-shaped nose positioned at the snout tip.

I'm refining positions: muzzle front edge, nose coordinates, lip pad spheres, and a lower jaw ellipsoid in cream with a joint point near the cheek, plus considering adding small teeth cones inside the mouth.

For the mouth I'm keeping it mostly closed and minimal, maybe adding a thin dark line to suggest the mouth seam, though it may end up hidden. For the eyes I'm placing small amber spheres with black pupils and darker brow ridges above, and I want to add a thin scar mark across the left eyebrow for character detail.

Working out scar placement...

Positioning the scar near the brow with slight rotation and adjusted depth so it doesn't sink into the surface. I'm adding round ears tucked into the mane with tawny coloring and dark inner shading, plus golden cheek tufts framing the face. For texture I'm scattering tiny black whisker-dot spheres along the muzzle in small clusters on each side.

Skipping a separate brow stripe for simplicity. For the paws, I'm adding small lighter-toned toe spheres on the front of each paw, offset slightly along the x-axis. I'm also working out the mane's layered cone placement so the tufts radiate outward and backward from the head center without obscuring the face, keeping cheek tufts positioned just outside the face edges.

Working out mane tuft layers across five radial rings, increasing in size and tuft count outward, totaling around 75 tufts with some jitter for natural variation, plus a core sphere filling the gap between the skull and the innermost tuft ring.

Checking that this core sphere doesn't accidentally cover the face—shrinking its z-scale so it stays behind the cheeks while still blending with the mane, then adding a second core ellipsoid near the chest/shoulders to extend the mane coverage downward.

Now I'm scattering individual tufts around the shoulders and under the chin for a chest ruff, each defined by a position, direction, length, and radius, then setting up a distance-based gradient from a focal point so tufts further from center fade toward a different color like gold at the tips.

I'm defining a piecewise gold-to-chocolate mane gradient with mix functions and added noise for natural variation, then building the tufts as low-poly flat-shaded cones before moving on to painting the body ellipsoids for the pelvis and chest.

Now I'm sweeping the tail along a chain with rounded caps and a darkened tip, carefully positioning the tail root so it connects smoothly into the hindquarters ellipsoid without poking through the body geometry.

I'm working out the torso proportions, placing the hindquarters, chest, and mid-belly ellipsoids and adjusting their y-position and scale so the bottoms line up consistently, while noting that countershading in the body paint already handles the cream underside so a separate belly shape isn't needed.

Now I'm setting up the skeleton: a root joint feeding into a three-point spine chain (spine1, spine2, chest), then a neck chain of two segments leading to the head joint, plus a jaw joint parented to the head for mouth articulation. I'm also mapping the torso mesh parts to their corresponding bones and adding a hidden neck mesh swept with tawny paint to blend under the mane.

Defining a helper for ellipsoid body parts that attaches sphere geometry to specific bones, using flat shading for the faceted low-poly body while keeping eyes smooth, then setting up the amber eye spheres with fine segmentation for a rounder look.

Mapping out the resting sphinx pose, I'm plotting the arm chain from shoulder through elbow and wrist down to the paw, tapering the radii along the way for a natural forelimb shape.

For the hind leg I'm positioning hip, knee, hock, and paw joints, but noticing the hock-to-paw segment might end up too short and overlap with the shin bone, so I need to adjust those z-coordinates to avoid the limbs intersecting.

Now I'm setting up the haunch and hind paw ellipsoid shapes with their scale parameters, planning the tail as a tapered chain sweep, and preparing imports for paint, mixing, smoothstep, noise, mottling, and countershading functions, plus a seeded RNG for jitter before writing the tuft helper function.

Still writing tuft code...

Checking the mane's bottom tufts stay near the chest without dipping too low, then I'm working out the shoulder tufts: 24 of them spread across the upper semicircle around the neck, with angles from -100° to 100° defining their position and direction radiating outward and down.

Now adding chest ruff tufts under the chin, 14 of them placed near the jawline pointing outward and down. With the mane geometry settled, I'm defining the color palette—tawny and cream tones with mottling and countershading for the body, and setting up similar mottled coloring for the limbs.

Moving on to the limb and head sweeps, using bone chains with tapered radius arrays and a cream muzzle. For the tail, I'm sweeping it down to a fine tip and adding a dark tuft at the end made of ellipsoids and fanned cones oriented along the tail's final direction.

Checking that paw bottoms sit flush at ground level so nothing sinks below zero.
